evidence_sentences.sentence: We show mass spectrometric data combined with data from enzymatic digestions that suggest the presence of a tetrasaccharide consisting of two N-acetylglucosamines, one galactose and one sialic acid, appearing on serum TF, is a biomarker of this particular CDG subtype.

In order to test whether other ALG1-CDG patients show these extra peaks, sera from ten more ALG1-CDG patients were analyzed and all showed these additional peaks, with a ratio over TF isoforms without the tetrasaccharide of 3.54 ± 1.99 % (range 0.8-6.7%).

In summary we show that a very small, but detectable portion of serum TF from all eleven patients with confirmed ALG1-CDG substitute a tetrasaccharide for the normal large glycan chain, possibly reflecting the nature of the deficient step in this particular subtype.
We suggest it may be useful as a biomarker of ALG1-CDG and that mass spectrometric analysis of serum TF directly can inform the physician of an ALG1 deficiency prior to genetic confirmation.
